record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.original_question: For homogeneous universes governed by the basic gravi-dilaton effective string action at tree level, with higher-order and loop corrections neglected, what are the detailed asymptotic limits of the corresponding NS-NS cosmological solutions, and are the known dilaton-moduli-vacuum and axion solutions asymptotically stable?

evidence.quote:
2.1 Asymptotics of speciﬁc tree-level string actions I
The aim here is to describe the detailed asymptotic limits of universes obeying the basic gravi-dilaton eﬀective string action, neglecting higher order and loop corrections. The plan to give a complete asymptotic analysis of the NS-NS models and ﬁrst results about the asymptotic stability of the known solutions (dilaton-moduli-vacuum and axion solutions).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider spatially homogeneous cosmological models derived from the tree-level gravi-dilaton low-energy effective action of string theory in the Neveu–Schwarz–Neveu–Schwarz (NS-NS) sector, with higher-derivative ($\alpha'$) corrections and string-loop corrections neglected. In the simplest setting, the relevant fields are a spacetime metric $g_{\mu\nu}$, a scalar dilaton $\phi$, and a pseudoscalar axion (Kalb–Ramond) field $\sigma$ dual to the NS-NS 2-form $B_{\mu\nu}$, with action (in the string frame)
$$S = \frac{1}{2\lambda_s^{d-1}} \int d^{d+1}x\, \sqrt{-g}\, e^{-\phi}\left( R + (\nabla\phi)^2 - \tfrac{1}{12} H_{\mu\nu\rho}H^{\mu\nu\rho}\right),$$
where $H = dB$. Restrict to homogeneous (e.g., Bianchi-type or anisotropic Kasner-like) backgrounds with metric of the form $ds^2 = -dt^2 + \sum_i a_i(t)^2 (dx^i)^2$, dilaton $\phi=\phi(t)$, and axion $\sigma=\sigma(t)$.

Two well-known exact families of solutions are:
(i) the dilaton–moduli–vacuum solutions, obtained for vanishing axion ($\sigma$ constant), which are generalized Kasner-type solutions with $a_i(t)\propto |t|^{p_i}$ and $e^{-\phi}\propto |t|^q$, parametrized by exponents satisfying $\sum_i p_i^2 + (1-\sum_i p_i)^2 = 1$;
(ii) the axion (rolling-axion) solutions, in which a nontrivial $\sigma(t)$ interpolates between two such Kasner-like asymptotic regimes.

Problems:
(a) Give a complete classification of the asymptotic limits (as the cosmological time approaches the initial or final singularity, or infinity) of all such homogeneous NS-NS solutions.
(b) Determine whether the dilaton–moduli–vacuum and axion solutions listed above are asymptotically stable as fixed points / asymptotic regimes of the associated dynamical system on the space of homogeneous backgrounds.
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search reveals active ongoing research on dynamical-systems classifications of asymptotic behaviour in tree-level string cosmologies and on the (partial) stability of saxion–axion fixed points. Some classifications of asymptotic behaviour for related gravi-dilaton/axion systems have appeared, and partial stability results are known, but a fully complete asymptotic analysis and stability characterization of all homogeneous NS-NS cosmological solutions, including the dilaton–moduli–vacuum and axion families, does not appear to have been definitively established in full generality.

status_evidence.title: From the string vacuum to FLRW or de Sitter via α' corrections
status_evidence.snippet: A dynamical systems analysis of the associated equations of motion results in a complete classification of their asymptotic behaviour.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work performs dynamical-systems classifications of asymptotic behaviour for string-cosmology equations of motion, indicating the problem is being actively studied.

status_evidence.title: Axion-Scalar Dynamics: from the Distance Conjecture to Cosmic Acceleration
status_evidence.snippet: The fixed point in the saxion–axion system is at most partially stable, in particular when the volume modulus and the axio-dilaton are taken into account.
status_evidence.claim: Stability of saxion–axion (dilaton–axion) fixed points is at most partial in current analyses, supporting only partial-results status.

status_evidence.title: Stabilizing dilaton and moduli vacua in string and M-theory cosmology
status_evidence.snippet: Stabilizing dilaton and moduli vacua in string and M-theory cosmology.
status_evidence.claim: Stabilization/stability of dilaton-moduli vacua in string cosmology has been studied but remains a topic of active investigation.
